claims.claim_text: A backup scheme keeps hourly RDB snapshots for the latest 48 hours and daily snapshots for one or two months.
claims.reasoning: The passages describe creating hourly and daily RDB snapshots and give the example retention periods.

citations.quote: Create a cron job in your server creating hourly snapshots of the RDB file in one directory, and daily snapshots in a different directory.

citations.quote: for instance you can take hourly snapshots for the latest 48 hours, and daily snapshots for one or two months.

claims.claim_text: That scheme implies as many as about 60 daily files.
claims.reasoning: Daily snapshots retained for one or two months entail roughly 30 to 60 daily files, with the maximum being about 60.

citations.quote: for instance you can take hourly snapshots for the latest 48 hours, and daily snapshots for one or two months.

claims.claim_text: At least once a day a snapshot should be transferred outside the data center, or at least outside the physical machine.
claims.reasoning: The passages explicitly recommend transferring an RDB snapshot at least once every day outside the data center or outside the physical machine.

citations.quote: At least one time every day make sure to transfer an RDB snapshot *outside your data center* or at least *outside the physical machine* running your Redis instance.

claims.claim_text: Redis can save the dataset every N seconds if there have been at least M changes.
claims.reasoning: The passages state that Redis can be configured to save the dataset every N seconds if there are at least M changes.

citations.quote: You can configure Redis to have it save the dataset every N seconds if there are at least M changes in the dataset

claims.claim_text: With a save point of 300 seconds and 100 changes, a crash can never lose more than five minutes of writes.
claims.reasoning: The passages say snapshots are usually created every five minutes or more and warn that the latest minutes of data may be lost; the save condition also requires both elapsed time and enough changes, so a hard maximum of five minutes is not supported.

citations.quote: for instance after at least five minutes and 100 writes against the data set, you can have multiple save points

However you'll usually create an RDB snapshot every five minutes or more, so in case of Redis stopping working without a correct shutdown for any reason you should be prepared to lose the latest minutes of data.
You can configure Redis to have it save the dataset every N seconds if there are at least M changes in the dataset
